Votre dette publique est passée de {a} %: Your public debt went from {a}% to {b}% of GDP. The mechanism is simple: every year in which the state spends more than it earns (your average deficit: {c}% of GDP), the shortfall is added to the debt. And the higher the debt, the heavier the interest to be paid — this is the "snowball effect", which makes recovery more and more difficult. For reference, the European rules (Maastricht criteria) aim for a deficit below 3% of GDP and debt below 60%.
Vous avez fait reculer la dette, de {a}: You reduced the debt, from {a}% to {b}% of GDP — that is rare and difficult. It requires a controlled deficit (yours: {c}% on average) and growth that "dilutes" the debt in a bigger GDP. Key rule: as soon as the deficit falls below ~3% of GDP, the debt tends to stabilise, then fall, when the economy is growing.
Votre dette est restée globalement stabl: Your debt remained broadly stable at around {a}% of GDP, with an average deficit of {b}%. Stabilising the debt without reducing it already avoids the snowball effect — but France remains well above the European thresholds (deficit 3%, debt 60%).
Emploi et croissance vont de pair (c'est: Jobs and growth go hand in hand (this is Okun's law): when activity speeds up, companies hire; when it slows down, unemployment rises. But not all levers work in the same way: investment and education feed tomorrow's growth (supply effect), while a big tax increase slows demand in the short term, and heavier contributions raise labour costs.
La société est restée apaisée (cohésion: Society remained peaceful (cohesion {a}/100). Social spending, public services and redistribution contribute to this: they reduce inequality and cushion crises.
La cohésion sociale s'est dégradée ({a}/: Social cohesion has deteriorated ({a}/100). Excessive cuts in benefits, public services or grants to local authorities fracture society and can trigger strikes and riots.
C'est l'arbitrage central du gouvernant: This is the central trade-off of governing: cutting spending puts the accounts in order, but every euro saved has a social cost for someone.
Votre intégrité a souffert ({a}/100). Cé: Your integrity has suffered ({a}/100). Giving in to lobbies or covering up an affair pays off in the short term, but undermines democratic trust: transparency protects better than secrecy, and scandals end up breaking — often at the worst moment.
Vous avez investi pour le climat ({a}/10: You invested in the climate ({a}/100): an immediate cost, but a long-term benefit — less energy dependence and a transition under way.
L'environnement a été négligé ({a}/100): The environment was neglected ({a}/100): short-term savings, but an ecological and health bill passed on to future generations.
Gouverner, c'est arbitrer. Un budget n'e: Governing means making trade-offs. A budget is never just a spreadsheet: every expense has to be funded, every saving has a social cost, every tax increase weighs on activity. There is no perfect choice, only balances to be found. A good leader is not the one who pleases everyone, but the one who reconciles sustainable accounts, jobs and the country's cohesion.
